ruling.recommended_action: Route to RydeHELP human review as a SAFE-1 safety/threat incident: provide the reviewer the verbatim chat log (F3–F5), the driver's statement (F6), the route/duration records (F1, F2) and both profiles (F7, F8); take no fare or account action automatically. Reviewer to determine (a) whether the 17:20 message was a genuine threat to confine the rider, and (b) any account consequence. Note the rider's recourse if medical assistance or a police report is needed (995 / RydeHELP) [SAFE-2 context].
ruling.escalation_reason: Threat-tagged driver chat message in a rider-filed safety dispute: chat #2 17:20 "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4], keyword-tagged as a threat [F5], sent one minute after the rider's 17:19 request to stop and get out [F3]; driver's account is that it was a safety instruction during a moving-vehicle door incident [F6]. No gps/timeline fact records locked doors or a stationary vehicle; route and duration records are normal (−0.1 km vs optimal [F1], +1.4 min [F2]). Reviewer to check: (1) whether the 17:20 message is a genuine threat to confine the rider; (2) any corroborating records (door/vehicle sensors, timeline events) for the driver's account in F6; (3) account consequences for either party given both profiles are clean [F7][F8]; no fare adjustment arises ($32.86 fixed RydeX fare, no deviation).

rejected_claims.reason: Rejected as a basis for adjudication: the driver's safety motive [F6] is a statement and under the system-records-prevail rule cannot override the verbatim chat message [F4] and its threat tag [F5]; in any event SAFE-1 escalates on the presence of a threat message in the record without weighing the stated motive.

Rejected as irrelevant to the safety claim: a non-aberrant route and normal duration [F1][F2] do not neutralize a threat-tagged chat message [F4][F5], and SAFE-1 attaches to the chat record, not to gps route metrics.

Rejected as irrelevant: no fare or route complaint arises here — the trip ran to the booked destination with actual 15.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal [F1][F2] and the RydeX fare is fixed so no RD-2 refund exists; the escalatable conduct is the 17:20 threat message [F4][F5], which RD-3/FARE-1 do not address.

Rejected only as to the requested outcome: the driver's clean 90-day record with 0 upheld disputes [F8] does not bar escalation, because RD-6's prior-upheld precondition is about repeated-violation flags, and SAFE-1 requires escalation on a single threat-tagged message [F4][F5]; no flag_account is imposed in any case.
Rejected only as to the requested outcome: the rider's clean profile [F7] removes any vexatious-claim suggestion but does not counteract the SAFE-1 escalation trigger in the chat record [F4][F5].

Not adopted as a finding: the 'confinement as leverage' reading is an inference beyond the record — the only record is the message itself [F4] with its tag [F5], and no gps/timeline fact shows locked doors or a held vehicle [F1][F2]; the weight of that inference is for the human reviewer under SAFE-1, not for this escalation summary.

Adopted as to the procedural outcome (escalate under SAFE-1 on threat message [F4][F5]) but its further assertion that a fare adjustment question exists is rejected: route is optimal at 15.4 km vs 15.5 km [F1] and the RydeX fare is fixed, so RD-2 yields no refundable amount.

Adopted as to scope: the driver has 0 upheld disputes in 90 days [F8], so the RD-6 repeated-breach precondition is not met and no flag_account is issued; any account review rests on this single escalated safety incident under SAFE-1.
